- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or volatile (alternating ±0.33), model often underestimates or overshoots mid-range; adjust downward if recent price dips, upward if sentiment rebounds.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overcorrects; cap forecast peak at 2–3% below true peak.  
- If 3+ consecutive days of low sentiment or negative sentiment history, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to account for mean reversion.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses 1–2% mean reversion in 10–15 day window; apply slight upward bias if sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish.  
- If sentiment history shows strong reversal (e.g., 0.00 → 1.00 or vice versa), model lags by 1–2 days; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to match sentiment shift.
